newsitem.title: UK: UK water watchdog defends regulators' record.
newsitem.headline: UK water watchdog defends regulators' record.

text.p: UK water industry watchdog chief Ian Byatt defended on Thursday the record of utility regulators and outlined their accountability at a conference on the industry organised by The Economist magazine.

"Regulators...have a good record," Byatt said, adding their actions "are checked by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) and judicial review and challenged by commentators, the media, consumer bodies and the regulated companies."
Regulators had economic objectives whereas sectoral and social considerations involved politicians, he said.
Byatt said it was "essential" to build up a consistent approach to utility regulation.
Byatt said he might consider broadening the consultation process but repeated his lukewarm response to the idea of a committee of regulators.
"Sources may need to be expanded but I think the analogy of a comany board with non-executive directors is not helpful," he said.
There have been calls recently for regulators to broaden the consultation process or for a committee of regulators who consulted on issues.
"A standing panel of non-specialist advisers could be sensible...so far I have preferred to rely on my customer service committee chairmen," Byatt told the conference.
He said he was in favour in principle of public hearings and would consider the issue at the next price review, but said "our experience of public consultation was not encouraging."
